items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Those were our stars that we’d hitched our wagons to. ... Max Roach.

ctx.x: What did being a bebopper mean?

Being a bebopper meant that you concerned yourself with certain elements of the music, like melody and chord changes, especially the chord changes, and rhythms where instead of the [Foster sings a repetitive drum pattern], the heavy four associated with the swing era, you had [Foster sings a widely varied rhythm], drummers dropping bombs. That became the expression used for the way drummers, Max Roach and Kenny Clarke, et cetera played. We liked the idea of playing with drummers who dropped bombs instead of…
